description: This grouped vertical bar chart illustrates the percentage point difference for various neural network configurations across two different models. The horizontal axis displays the categorical configurations, labeled from left to right as "hidden:[50], linear", "hidden:[], linear", "hidden:[100], ReLU", and "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU", with no specific sorting applied. The vertical axis represents the "% point difference" on a linear scale, ranging from -0.2 to 0.2 with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.1, and includes a solid horizontal baseline at 0.0. Each category on the horizontal axis contains a pair of bars placed side-by-side. According to the legend in the top right corner, the lighter grey-blue bars represent the "mBERT" model, and the darker blue bars represent the "XLM-R" model. All bars are outlined with a thin black border. For the "hidden:[50], linear" category, mBERT shows a value of approximately -0.20 (the lowest value on the chart), while XLM-R is around -0.06. In the "hidden:[], linear" category, both models show positive values, with mBERT at roughly 0.09 and XLM-R reaching the highest positive value on the chart at approximately 0.21. For "hidden:[100], ReLU", mBERT is near -0.11 and XLM-R is slightly positive at about 0.02. Finally, for the "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU" category, both models are negative, with mBERT at approximately -0.18 and XLM-R at -0.14.
